title: MDVT: Enhancing Multimodal Recommendation with Model-Agnostic Multimodal-Driven Virtual Triplets

problem.claim: Data sparsity hinders recommender-system performance because traditional models rely on limited historical interactions to learn user preferences and item properties.

gap.claim: Existing multimodal recommendation methods often use multimodal information only as side information and do not fully leverage its potential.

contributions.claim: MDVT is a model-agnostic approach that constructs multimodal-driven virtual triplets to provide supervision signals for mitigating data sparsity in multimodal recommendation.
MDVT introduces static, dynamic, and hybrid warm-up threshold strategies for producing high-quality virtual triplets.
After the warm-up threshold is satisfied, MDVT uses virtual triplets with an enhanced pair-wise loss for joint model optimization without significant gradient skew.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive experiments on multiple real-world datasets reportedly show that integrating MDVT into advanced multimodal recommendation models alleviates data sparsity and improves recommendation performance.
The reported performance improvements are particularly pronounced in sparse-data scenarios.

narrative_sequence.summary: Existing methods do not fully exploit multimodal information.
MDVT constructs multimodal-driven virtual triplets and provides three warm-up threshold strategies.
The selected warm-up threshold enables joint optimization with an enhanced pair-wise loss while avoiding significant gradient skew.
Experiments on multiple real-world datasets report improved recommendation performance, especially under sparse data.

source_observation.claim: The hybrid warm-up strategy first uses dynamic adjustment to locate an approximate optimum and then refines it with static search in a narrow hyper-parameter space.

interpretation.claim: A coarse-to-fine tuning procedure can trade off search efficiency and optimization quality.

application.claim: Use adaptive search to identify a promising region before applying more expensive refinement.

exception.claim: Dynamic adjustment may miss optimal performance, while exhaustive static search may be computationally intensive.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative improvements.
The abstract does not provide construction details for the virtual triplets or the enhanced pair-wise loss.
The abstract does not report computational costs or reproducibility details.
